'''Buyisiwe Sondezi''' is a South African physicist. She was the first woman in Africa to obtain a [[Doctor of Philosophy]] (PhD) in experimental physics of highly correlated matter when she graduated at [[University of Johannesburg]] on 23 September 2014.<ref name="From a rural school to challenging established Physics theory - UJ woman Physics researcher Buyisiwe Sondezi">{{Cite news | title = From a rural school to challenging established Physics theory - UJ woman Physics researcher Buyisiwe Sondezi | website = [[University of Johannesburg]] | date = 20 October 2014 | url = http://www.uj.ac.za/EN/Newsroom/News/Pages/From-a-rural-school-to-challenging-established-Physics-theory---UJ-woman-Physics-researcher-Buyisiwe-Sondezi.aspx | access-date = 21 October 2014 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20141024165606/http://www.uj.ac.za/EN/Newsroom/News/Pages/From-a-rural-school-to-challenging-established-Physics-theory---UJ-woman-Physics-researcher-Buyisiwe-Sondezi.aspx | archive-date = 24 October 2014 | url-status = dead | df = dmy-all }}</ref>

==Academic life==
Buyisiwe is the first born child and a sister of ten siblings.<ref name="
GirlPower celebrates women in Science, Engineering and Technology">{{Cite news | title = 
GirlPower celebrates women in Science, Engineering and Technology | website = [[University of South Africa]] | date = 21 August 2013| url = http://www.unisa.ac.za/cset/news/index.php/2013/08/girlpower-celebrates-women-in-science-engineering-and-technology/ }}</ref> She grew up in [[Newcastle, KwaZulu-Natal|Newcastle]] and learnt science at a rural school. The school had no laboratory. "I had to picture how things are, because the school had no lab. I was just told if you mix 'one' and 'two' you get a 'three'. We relied on what the textbook said," says Dr Sondezi. She saw laboratory equipment for the first time while studying towards her degree at [[Vista University]] in Soweto, which is now part of the University of Johannesburg. Buyisiwe graduated with a [[Bachelor of Science]] (BSc) in Physics, Chemistry and Statistics.<ref name="From a rural school to challenging established Physics theory - UJ woman Physics researcher Buyisiwe Sondezi"/>

Buyisiwe worked briefly as a teacher at [[Sandringham High School, Johannesburg]] in 2003. In 2005, she lectured Fundamental Physics class at [[Rand Afrikaans University]] and demonstrated the second year Physics Practicals at the same university.<ref name="Dr Buyisiwe Sondezi">''Departmental Staff: University of Johannesburg'' in [[University of Johannesburg]] accessed at [http://www.uj.ac.za/EN/Faculties/science/departments/physics/about/DepartmentalStaff/AucklandPark/Pages/MissBuyisiweMhlungu.aspx Dr Buyisiwe Sondezi] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120505070742/http://www.uj.ac.za/EN/Faculties/science/departments/physics/about/DepartmentalStaff/AucklandPark/Pages/MissBuyisiweMhlungu.aspx# |date=5 May 2012 }} on 21 October 2014.</ref>

She holds a Honours and master's degrees in physics, researching properties of solar cells. She started her PhD in the same direction, however, she switched the topic of her doctorate to highly correlated matter in experimental physics in 2007.<ref name="From a rural school to challenging established Physics theory - UJ woman Physics researcher Buyisiwe Sondezi"/>

[[South African Nuclear Energy Corporation]] (NECSA) employed her as a [[scientist]] in the Radiation Utilisation Division between 2005 and 2007. In 2007, she started working for University of Johannesburg as a lecturer.<ref name="UJ researcher first female physicist in her field in Africa">{{Cite news  | title = UJ researcher first female physicist in her field in Africa | website = [[Engineering News (Creamer Media)]]  | date = 20 October 2014 | url = http://www.engineeringnews.co.za/article/uj-researcher-first-female-physicist-in-her-field-in-africa-2014-10-20}}</ref>

In 2009, she won the Department of Science and Technology's women in Science award<ref name="Dr Buyisiwe Sondezi"/> and was nominated as one of Cosmopolitan magazine's "Fun and Fearless Women".<ref name="Mail & Guardian 200 Young South Africans - Science and Technology Buyisiwe Sondezi">{{Cite news | title = Mail & Guardian 200 Young South Africans - Science and Technology Buyisiwe Sondezi | website = [[Mail & Guardian 200 Young South Africans]] | date = 2012 | url = http://ysa2012.mg.co.za/buyisiwe-sondezi/ | access-date = 21 October 2014 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20141024140841/http://ysa2012.mg.co.za/buyisiwe-sondezi-mhlungu/ | archive-date = 24 October 2014 | url-status = dead }}</ref>

In 2012, she was named one of [[Mail & Guardian]]'s 200 Young South Africans, in the Science and Technology category.<ref name="Mail & Guardian 200 Young South Africans - Science and Technology Buyisiwe Sondezi"/>

Buyisiwe made news headlines as the first woman in Africa to earn a PhD in her field in October 2014.

{{blockquote|The study is based on cerium-based compounds and intermetallic systems which feature within the broad class of strongly correlated electron systems (SCES). The temperature dependence of physical properties in the vicinity of a quantum critical point (QCP) opens up a realm of new and unexplored physics. Research into quantum critical phenomena is not only conducive to a study of new physics in its own right, but is expected to lead to a much broader understanding of the complex yet fundamental behavior of elementary particles in metals and the cooperative phenomena in them that lead to the wide variety of useful applications of intermetallics in everyday life. The problem at the center of this work is the new and unknown temperature- and field-dependencies of physical properties (electronic transport, thermal transport, magnetic and thermodynamic properties) in localized magnetic systems when brought to quantum criticality.<ref name="Description of the study">{{cite web |title=Short description of the study |url=http://www.uj.ac.za/EN/Faculties/science/departments/physics/about/DepartmentalStaff/AucklandPark/Pages/MissBuyisiweMhlungu.aspx |access-date=21 October 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120505070742/http://www.uj.ac.za/EN/Faculties/science/departments/physics/about/DepartmentalStaff/AucklandPark/Pages/MissBuyisiweMhlungu.aspx |archive-date=5 May 2012 |url-status=dead |df=dmy-all }}</ref>}}

She has written publications in collaboration with various physicists based around the globe.<ref name="Dr Buyisiwe Sondezi"/>

In her spare time, she tutors Mathematics and Science to pupils.<ref name="Buyisiwe breaks barriers">{{Cite news | title = Buyisiwe breaks barriers | website = [[Destiny (magazine)|Destiny]] connect | date = 21 October 2014 | url = http://www.destinyconnect.com/2014/10/21/buyisiwe-breaks-barriers/ | access-date = 21 October 2014 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20141029220831/http://www.destinyconnect.com/2014/10/21/buyisiwe-breaks-barriers/ | archive-date = 29 October 2014 | url-status = dead }}</ref>
